category: open-access full-text article corpus (public S3 bucket) with E-utilities and OAI-PMH APIs

free_tier.stated: The PMC Article Datasets are free on AWS through an HTTPS or S3 URL with no log-in; E-utilities allow 3 requests a second per IP address without an API key and 10 a second with a free key; the OAI-PMH service allows 3 requests a second with no concurrent requests
free_tier.notes: The bucket itself publishes no request or byte cap; the request limits are those of the E-utilities and OAI-PMH services. An anonymous esearch on 2026-10-30 answered x-ratelimit-limit 3.

per_object_cap.stated: one prefix per article version holding its files; ESearch returns at most 10,000 records per query, and the daily inventory CSV has no record limit

retention.stated: the bucket is live: a removed article version's prefix and files are deleted with no notification, detectable only by reconciling the daily inventory; inventory reports are kept 30 days; the legacy baseline packages on FTP and the Cloud Service were removed the week of August 24, 2026

egress.terms: Free: NLM provides the bucket through the AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program without charge, over HTTPS or S3, with no log-in.

interface_detail: S3 bucket pmc-oa-opendata (arn:aws:s3:::pmc-oa-opendata) read with --no-sign-request, or https://pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/ over HTTPS, with a daily S3 inventory CSV; E-utilities at https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/ (esearch with open access[filter]); OAI-PMH at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/api/oai/v1/mh/; BioC API. The PMC OA Web Service is no longer available and there are no baseline bulk packages.
tooling: aws s3 cp or sync with --no-sign-request, or curl over HTTPS; the daily inventory CSV as the list of article versions; EDirect to page past 10,000 ESearch results
chaining: The bucket is the bulk path: objects for roughly 8 million article versions, listed in a daily inventory CSV with no record limit; an esearch on open access[filter] counted 8357213 records on 2026-10-30; E-utilities or OAI-PMH select articles by date or licence before the S3 fetch.

limits.value: E-utilities: more than 3 requests a second per IP address without an API key answers an error; up to 10 a second by default with a key
OAI-PMH: 3 requests a second, no concurrent requests
ESearch: at most 10,000 returned records per query

binding_note: The bucket publishes no request or byte cap and needs no key; the 3 a second E-utilities limit binds only on selection, which the daily inventory replaces.

identity_cost.detail: No account or key for the bucket: it is read without any log-in. An E-utilities key, for 10 requests a second, comes from the Settings page of an NCBI account, which signs in through federated logins such as Login.gov, Google, Microsoft live.com, ORCiD or an institution.

reliability_note: Removed article versions vanish from the bucket with no notification; exceeding the E-utilities limits can get an IP address blocked from NCBI.
confidence_note: The bucket terms, the inventory and the API limits are NLM pages. An anonymous HTTPS GET of one article's full-text XML answered 200 with 109,974 bytes on 2026-10-31, and the bucket README answered 200 to an anonymous request; the E-utilities and OAI-PMH limits are documented, not measured.
